== Biography ==
'''Hugh Glasgow''' was born about 1829 in County Antrim, Ireland. His 1852 marriage record directly names his father as [[Glasgow-3956|Hugh Glasgow]], a weaver.<ref name="Marriage1852">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1852/09422/5413278.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], entry 49, Hugh Glasgow and Anne Wilson, 24 December 1852.</ref>

Hugh was a 23-year-old bachelor, weaver and resident of Liminary when he married [[Cushnehan-1|'''Anne Cushnehan''']], the 25-year-old widow of a man named Wilson, on 24 December 1852. Anne lived at Tully and was a daughter of Hugh Cushnehan, weaver.<ref name="Marriage1852" />

Anne Glasgow died at Liminary on 14 March 1877. The register describes her as married, aged 54 and a weaver's wife; Nathaniel Glasgow was present at her death.<ref name="AnnDeath1877">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1877/020560/7214822.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], entry 162, Ann Glasgow, 14 March 1877, Liminary.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3956]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The held 1852 civil marriage account directly names Hugh Glasgow, weaver as the father of Hugh, 23, a Liminary weaver. That record-defined father fits the selected Hugh profile; the junior man’s unproved 1889 death and the elder Hugh’s parentage are separate.

Held citation and associated historical narrative address this selected father-child identity; no original was newly inspected.

Next useful test: Compare the full 1852 father line with Eliza’s 1854 marriage.

Source basis already held: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1852/09422/5413278.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register (https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1852/09422/5413278.pdf), entry 49, Hugh Glasgow and Anne Wilson, 24 December 1852.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



=== Identity ===

This Hugh was not [[Glasgow-2998|the unmarried Roman Catholic labourer recorded at Maghereagh in 1901]]. He was also distinct from [[Glasgow-2599|Hugh Glasgow of Nova Scotia]], who had formed a family there by 1876 while Anne remained a married weaver's wife at Liminary in 1877.

A Hugh Glasgow who died in the Ballymena registration district on 8 June 1889 was a 55-year-old widowed weaver. He is a strong candidate for this man, but the death entry supplies no relative or residence that securely bridges him to the 1852 marriage, so the death has not been attached as certain.<ref name="HughDeath1889">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1889/06144/4755156.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], entry 301, Hugh Glasgow, 8 June 1889.</ref>

=== Family ===

Nathaniel Glasgow, the informant at Anne's death, was probably a son or other close relative. The register does not state his relationship, so he has not been attached as a child.

A Hugh Glasgow, aged 55, died in the Ballymena registration district on 8 June 1889.<ref name="DeathIndex1889">[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death General Register Office for Northern Ireland, civil death index], Hugh Glasgow, 8 June 1889, Ballymena registration district, D/1889/23/1004/9/301.</ref>
